study.question: With task routing, observed direct pools and ordinal action summaries held fixed, is one aligned target-match action-summary copy sufficient, and does erasing both reproduce the loss from rotating both? This is a follow-up on redundant feedback representation, not a new task-conditioning interaction estimate.
study.hypothesis: The raw target-match action summary and its norm-scaled/gated copy offer redundant aligned feedback. The r0031 small individual rotation losses but larger joint loss reflect rescue by the surviving aligned copy. Retaining either aligned copy while zeroing the other should largely preserve click AUC; removing both should reduce it. The raw-only candidate tests a simpler action representation. The inherited global optimum is retained as a utility reference, not replaced based on this hypothesis. The scaled copy is only redundant where its inherited support is active: _coarse_extension_coefficients also requires at least four occupied blocks plus nondegenerate coefficient norms. On inactive support, the scaled copy is zero while the raw copy may survive. Consequently whole-population interchangeable sufficiency is stronger than active-support redundancy, and raw-only versus scaled-only can be asymmetric.

study.proposed_difference: Add match_action_availability in {both,raw,scaled,none}. After the inherited alignment selector, use a five-row Boolean torch.where gate solely on action coordinates: both=(1,1,1,1,1), raw=(1,1,1,1,0), scaled=(0,1,1,1,1), none=(0,1,1,1,0). Original summary_rotation_group=none retains alignment. All cells execute identical contractions/gather/selector/gate shapes; no new learned state, loss, masks, scorer population, data or optimizer change. Candidate keeps only raw match action content. Four fresh cells form the complete erasure factorial.
predictions: Primary directional prediction: A_both > A_none; retaining raw or scaled alone recovers most of that gap. Operational descriptive criterion fixed before scoring: both single-copy cells lose less than 0.0010 AUC relative to both, the none cell loses at least 0.0015, and I=A_both-A_raw-A_scaled+A_none < -0.0010. These cutoffs are effect-size decision rules, not significance tests or equivalence margins.

At fixed nonzero residual state, erasure changes only selected match action coordinates and downstream outputs. All original item/ordinal summaries, match counts, coefficients, compression assignments, pool/scorer outputs, masks, state keys and initializer order remain identical.

The new none endpoint is expected to approximate existing g1-r0028-pool_ordinal_task (AUC0.6637536617254408) and g1-r0031-rotate_both_match_task (0.6637318310781741); this descriptive closeness is already observed, not a new forecast. The new neither/both reruns establish fresh graph-matched endpoints; they do not count as independent repetitions.

On inputs with inactive fifth support, scaled-only and none have identical match-action content at a common fixed state; raw-only and both have identical match-action content there. On active support the two retained summaries are proportional in exact arithmetic. Verify this algebraically/numerically in host preflight, and log active-support/raw-nonzero-fifth-zero prevalence. If authorized support-conditioned validation is not exposed, use existing history bins as exploratory proxies only and leave coverage attribution unresolved.
falsifiers: On active scaled support, if removing either copy is as harmful as removing both, the redundant-rescue explanation is weakened; distinct scaling, optimization or complementarity is more plausible. Whole-population scaled-only loss can also reflect absent fifth support: this refutes unconditional interchangeability but not active-support redundancy. If support-conditioned scoring is unavailable, keep that distinction unresolved.
If double erasure preserves quality but double rotation loses quality, misleading rotated cues or optimization interference is more plausible than loss of aligned information.
If neither erasure cell loses quality, the apparent rotation dependence does not demonstrate necessity of these summary channels; retain the null result.

If host correctness or ancestor bridge checks fail, especially item/ordinal paths, mask/partition invariance, sparse gradients or optimizer updates, do not attribute differences to the declared availability contrast.

Effects that do not repeat under an authorized paired-seed follow-up remain single-seed observations. No total historical-action effect, task-routing interaction or production-time causal claim follows from this suite.
alternative_explanations: Erasure preserves nominal parameter count but removes effective input directions and their gradients; it does not match effective capacity or gradient geometry. Earlier rotated-action trials are information-preserving nuisance controls, conditional on bridges.

Raw and scaled summaries are proportional only at fixed input and active support in exact arithmetic; sample-dependent scaling, BF16 reductions, support degeneracies and optimizer conditioning can affect learning.

Action information remains in ordinal summaries, direct pools and frozen action-derived partitions. This is conditional match-summary dependence, not total action removal or a causal user-response effect.
One fixed training seed and repeated user exposures; fresh endpoint reruns are graph controls, not independent replications.
Weak individual effects can be ordinary seed/validation variation. Nonadditivity of an AUC statistic is not itself proof of a mechanistic interaction.
The model-selection objective sacrifices auxiliary-task quality relative to DIN; click gains cannot be described as uniformly improved multitask performance.

Inherited fifth-direction coarse-extension gating requires at least four occupied blocks and nondegenerate cubic/scrambled/incumbent/position norms. Raw action information can exist where the scaled copy is zero; worse scaled-only performance on such inputs is gate coverage, not evidence of two complementary active directions. Do not infer this explanation without support prevalence and slice evidence.
